subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw ship native backup exclude-pattern controls in core now, and what default/protected-path policy should that CLI contract use?
rationale: The missing capability is source-reproducible, but defaults and protected recovery paths decide the balance between backup size, sensitive-file avoidance, and restorable archives.

options.title: Review linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest compatibility, and proof before landing or narrowing it.

options.title: Narrow to explicit excludes first
options.body: Accept only `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` while deferring smart defaults and auto-detected ignore files until restore-safety expectations are clearer.

options.title: Decline native excludes for now
options.body: Keep core backups coarse, document the current scope, and direct optional backup strategies such as Keep My Claw to ClawHub after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest compatibility, and proof before landing or narrowing it.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original backup CLI PR and are listed for CLI ownership, making them the strongest routing signal for this core CLI contract decision.
